Definition: from G820; to render infamous, i.e. (by implication) contemn or maltreat:--despise, dishonour, suffer shame, entreat shamefully.
BiblicalUsage: To dishonour is to treat as worthless, and the word cuts both ways in the New Testament. The apostles rejoiced that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for His name, the rich dishonour the poor in James's charge, the tenants dishonoured the vineyard owner's servants, and Jesus answered the charge of having a devil by saying, I honour my Father, and ye do dishonour me.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe dishonour reveals what a person truly values, because the apostles counted shame for Christ an honour and the world counts honour for Christ a shame. The two scales will never agree, and I hold that God's weighing is the one that lasts.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; James, Brother of the Lord; Paul
